number.why: The source explicitly reports 39/133 for Lactobacillus GG and 40/134 for placebo. These support the reconstructed RR, rather than a source-reported RR or CI. The endpoint is diarrhea within 21 days after enrollment. ITT is explicitly stated, but the reported denominators do not cover all 302 randomized patients; the ruling acknowledges this limitation.

quotes.span: Diarrhea developed in 39 (29.3%) of 133 patients randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG and in 40 (29.9%) of 134 patients randomized to receive placebo (P=.93).
The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who developed diarrhea in the first 21 days after enrollment.
Results were analyzed in an intention-to-treat fashion.
302 hospitalized patients receiving antibiotics were randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG, 20 x 10(9) CFU/d, or placebo for 14 days.

entry.why: The randomized entry population explicitly comprised patients receiving antibiotics, matching the question. Lactobacillus GG was compared with placebo.
